headline: Approved $1.5mil for Fire, $1.1mil for police, and a $180,430 PEG Fund transfer; amended 278 Middlesex Street JAM Plan.
summary: A vote of 8-2 set a review of executive session minutes on the Flock camera system. A motion to cut the PEG Fund transfer to $152,000 failed 3-6. Requests on the Hunts Falls on-ramp, Bicentennial Park, and the ICC were referred to the City Manager.
decisions: Placed on file the communication about remote Zoom participation.
Placed on file the Breast Cancer Awareness proclamation.
Placed on file the citation honoring Kolthyda (Nina) Hok.
Placed on file the October 20 minutes of the Non-Profit Organization SC and City Council meetings.
Referred to the City Manager a request to identify underutilized downtown public spaces for possible improvements.
Referred to the City Manager a request for information on when Bicentennial Park on Jackson Street will open.
Referred to the City Manager a request to examine the Hunts Falls rotary on-ramp from Centralville, including yield signage.
Referred to the City Manager a request for a public Flock Camera demonstration with a question-and-answer session.
Approved a review for possible release of executive session minutes on the Flock Camera System, 8-2.
Referred to the City Manager a request for a letter opposing the ICC being used as any type of shelter.
Referred to the City Manager a request for a report on the yearly cost of a property tax freeze for seniors over 75.
Placed on file the Tree Committee October 2026 update.
Placed on file the Father Maguire motion response.
Placed on file the 105 Market Street motion response.
Placed on file the Non-Profit PILOT letter response.
Placed on file the Traffic Ordinance informational report.
Placed on file the Career Center performance report for FY2026.
Approved appointments of Jennifer Guilbeault to the Community Preservation Committee and Timothy Hovey to the Zoning Board of Appeals, 10-0.
Referred MRF FY2027 to a public hearing on November 10, 2026 at 7 PM after first reading.
Approved the amendment to the JAM Plan for 278 Middlesex Street, 10-0.
Approved a $1.5mil supplemental appropriation for Fire, 10-0.
Approved the $180,430 PEG Fund transfer, 7-2.
Failed: a motion to cut the PEG Fund transfer to $152,000.00 was defeated, 3-6 with one recusal.
Approved the $1.1mil Free Cash transfer for police, 7-3.
Withdrawn: a motion to refer the $1.1mil Free Cash transfer to the Finance SC was withdrawn.
Accepted the Non-Profit Organization SC report as a report of progress.
Referred two property damage claims to the Law Department for a report and recommendation.
Referred a request about a tree encroaching on 38 Foch Street to the City Manager and DPW.
Referred the gas main replacement at 61 Durant Street to a public hearing on November 10, 2026 at 7 PM.
Referred the gas main installation on Old Ferry Road to a public hearing on November 10, 2026 at 7 PM.
Referred the gas main replacement on 18th Street to a public hearing on November 10, 2026 at 7 PM.
Referred the handhole installation in front of 114 Merrimack Street to a public hearing on November 10, 2026 at 7 PM.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
Date:       October 27, 2026
Time:        6:30 PM
Location: City Council Chamber, 375 Merrimack Street, 2nd Floor, 
Lowell, MA / Zoom (Hybrid)
1. ROLL CALL
Roll Call showed 10 present (C. Chau, C. Descoteaux, M. Gitschier, C. 
Juran, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. Mercier, C. Nuon, C. Robinson, C. 
Scott).
M. Gitschier presiding.
At the conclusion of the meeting C. Descoteaux offered a moment of 
silence in darkened chamber for Maureen Keene, wife of Interim Fire Chief 
David Keene.  
2. MAYOR'S BUSINESS
2.1. Communication Remote / Zoom Participation.
In City Council, Motion “To accept and place on file” by C. Scott, seconded 
by C. Chau.  So voted.
2.2. Proclamation - Breast Cancer Awareness.
In City Council, Motion “To accept and place on file” by C. Descoteaux, 
seconded by C. Juran.  So voted.  M. Gitschier read the proclamation.
2.3. Citation - Kolthyda (Nina) Hok.
In City Council, Motion “To accept and place on file” by C. Chau, seconded 
by C. McDonough.  So voted.  M. Gitschier read the citation noting Ms. 
Hok’s journey to becoming a business owner (Nails Express) in the City.  
Ms. Hok thanked the Council and noted her appreciation.  C. Chau 
recognized the accomplishments of Ms. Hok.

3.1. Minutes of Non-Profit Organization SC October 20th; City Council 
Regular Meeting October 20th, for acceptance.
In City Council, Motion “To accept and place on file” by C. Liang, seconded 
by C. Juran.  So voted.
4. CITY COUNCIL - MOTIONS
4.1. C. McDonough - Req. City Mgr. have the appropriate departments 
work with community partners such as the LDNA, small businesses, 
event organizers, and others to identify underutilized public spaces 
and explore potential improvements to increase foot traffic in and 
around the downtown. 
In City Council, seconded by C. Liang, referred to City Manager.  So voted.
C. McDonough noted the number of ideas that are suggested for use and 
that they should be organized so that some can assist with using City for 
property for open space.  C. Robinson suggested open space use for part 
of City property on Market Street.  C. Robinson noted downtown area is a 
neighborhood.  
4.2. C. McDonough - Req. City Mgr. provide information regarding the 
anticipated opening of the Bicentennial Park on Jackson Street.
In City Council, seconded by C. Mercier, referred to City Manager.  So 
voted.  C. McDonough noted it was approved green space that needs to be 
open to the public.  
Motion by C. Nuon, seconded by C. Liang to take Item #6.5 out of order.  
So voted.  
4.3. C. Robinson - Req. City Mgr. have the proper department examine
and address through proper channels the on-ramp leading to the 
Hunts Falls rotary from Centralville, including yield signage.
In City Council, seconded by C. Mercier, referred to City Manager.  So 
voted.  C. Robinson noted this was a hot button issue for residents.  C.

Juran questioned what the issue was in the area, noting she did not notice 
any.  C. Robinson described the challenges and noted the number of 
complaints by the residents of the City.  
4.4. C. Robinson / C. Descoteaux - Req. City Mgr. have the proper 
departments work together to offer a public Flock Camera 
demonstration with a question-and-answer session.
In City Council, no second needed, referred to City Manager.  So voted.  
Registered speaker, Ron Peacetree (comment – noted concerns with the 
system and how the company uses it, must follow legal protocol) and 
Joseph Boyle (comment – noted the need for an open process for residents 
and not to force it upon them), addressed the body.  C. Robinson 
commented on his review of the system and the process by the police and 
that it is helpful to law enforcement.  C. Descoteaux commented on the 
presentation by the Lowell Police and that the company could be added as 
well for presentations.  C. Descoteaux commented on the audit protections 
in the system and that it was a deterrent to crime.  C. Nuon noted public 
information builds trust.  C. McDonough noted a public conversation must 
be done.  C. McDonough questioned the release of recent executive 
session minutes regarding Flock.  M. Gitschier outlined the process.  
Motion by C. McDonough, seconded by C. Nuon to review for possible 
release executive session minutes regarding use of the Flock Camera 
System by Law Department and City Council.  Adopted per Roll Call vote 8 
yeas (C. Chau, C. Juran, M. Gitschier, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. Nuon, 
C. Robinson, C. Scott), 2 nays (C. Descoteaux, C. Mercier).  So voted.  City
Solicitor Williams noted review by the Law Department is necessary as a 
step to release such minutes and that they are confidential until release.  C.
Robinson indicated that another executive session is forthcoming regarding 
Flock and questioned if release would be proper.  C. Juran noted a process
must be developed regarding release of the executive minutes.  C. Chau 
questioned if he could vote to release minutes if he was not at the executive
session.  City Solicitor Williams indicated he could.  C. Mercier noted topic 
was in executive session and that the motion should be referred there.  
Chair released to Vice Chair Nuon at 8:45 PM.  M. Gitschier questioned bid 
process for this vendor and noted that they should not be at any 
presentation as it would just be a sales pitch.  Chair returned at 8:47 PM.  
C. Robinson noted first step is to have the police provide public 
demonstration of Flock.

4.5. C. Robinson / M. Gitschier - Req. City Mgr. and the Council send a
letter clearly stating opposition to repurposing the ICC into any type 
of shelter due to the City’s economic and developmental goals and 
objectives.
In City Council, no second needed, referred to City Manager.  So voted.  
Registered speaker, Ron Peacetree (comment – gave economics of using 
the ICC for a shelter and that the need will be there), addressed the 
Council.  Chair released to Vice Chair Nuon at 8:50 PM.  M. Gitschier noted
UML owns the site and that they have a process and a plan for it which 
does not seem to be for a shelter based upon meeting with UML Chacellor 
Chen.  Chair returned at 9:00 PM.  C. Robinson noted the need for clear 
information.  C. McDonough noted it was a false headline and that they 
must know the UML process.  
4.6. M. Gitschier - Req. City Mgr. provide the City Council with a report
on the yearly cost of providing a freeze on property tax increases for 
any senior citizen over the age of 75 who have lived in and owned 
their current residence for more than 30 years.
In City Council, seconded by C. Nuon, referred to City Manager.  So voted.
C. Juran commented on the motion indicating that there are many variables
that may affect people and that there should be possible reimbursement 
when property is sold.  Chair released to Vice Chair Nuon at 9:06 PM.  M. 
Gitschier noted with every legislation there are always others who wants it 
and that possible reimbursement may be favorable.  Chair returned at 9:10 
PM.  C. Scott recognized the difficulty in administering it and that seniors 
should be made aware of all programs available to them.  C. McDonough 
noted the available programs to the seniors.  
5. COMMUNICATIONS FROM CITY MANAGER
5.1. Motion Responses.
A) Motion Response - Tree Committee October 2026 Update - In City 
Council, Motion “To accept and place on file” by C. McDonough, seconded 
by C. Mercier.  So voted.  Chair released to Vice Chair Nuon at 9:12 PM.  
M. Gitschier noted language should say regulatory and advisory powers to 
committee.  Chair returned at 9:15 PM.  C. Robinson noted appointments 
are approved by Council.  
B) Motion Response - Father Maguire - In City Council, Motion “To

exercise equipment will be available in the future which is a great start.  C.

C. Juran noted the need to know how projects are prioritized for completion

C) Motion Response - 105 Market Street - In City Council, Motion “To

C. McDonough commented on improvements in the area and that police 
calls have increased over the years and that should be addressed.  C. 
Descoteaux questioned when report regarding bars versus restaurants 
licenses will be available.  City Solicitor Williams indicated next meeting will

the first step as there is a need for funding.
5.2. Informational Reports
Informational Report - Traffic Ordinance - In City Council, Motion “To 
accept and place on file” by C. Mercier, seconded by C. Nuon.  So voted.  
C. Juran asked about the new business on Loring Street.
Informational Report - Career Center Performance FY2026 - In City 
Council, Motion “To accept and place on file” by C. Mercier, seconded by 
C. Nuon.  So voted.  Shawn Machado (Asst. City Manager) highlighted 
portions of the report noting the number of clients served along with the 
meeting of goals set by the organization.  Mr. Machado noted the efforts of 
the staff and director, Nancy Gagnon.  C. Juran questioned aspects of the 
report.  Ms. Gagnon commented on differences in ratings.  C. Robinson 
noted the report and indicated that area will suffer more job losses.  Mr. 
Machado noted the recent award to Ms. Gagnon.  C. Scott recognized the 
effort of the department.  M. Gitschier thanked the organization.  
5.3. Communication - Appointment of New Members to Various 
Boards and Commissions.

6. VOTES FROM THE CITY MANAGER
6.1. Vote - MRF FY2027.
In City Council, Given 1st Reading.  Motion to refer to Public Hearing on 
November 10, 2026 @ 7 PM by C. Nuon, seconded by C. Liang.  So voted.
6.2. Vote - Amend JAM Plan - 278 Middlesex Street.
In City Council, Given 2nd reading.  Motion “To Adopt” by C. Nuon, 
seconded by C. McDonough.  Adopted per Roll Call vote 10 yeas (C. Chau,
C. Descoteaux, M. Gitschier, C. Juran, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. 
Mercier, C. Nuon, C. Robinson, C. Scott).  So voted.  Ms. Baez-Rose 
commented on the change and the need for the change which would be 
developed by Heritage Properties.  
6.3. Vote - $1.5mil Supplemental Appropriation – Fire.
In City Council, Given 2nd reading.  Motion “To Adopt” by C. Mercier, 
seconded by C. Chau.  Adopted per Roll Call vote 10 yeas (C. Chau, C. 
Descoteaux, M. Gitschier, C. Juran, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. Mercier, 
C. Nuon, C. Robinson, C. Scott).  So voted.  C. Juran questioned the tax 
implications.  Conor Baldwin (CFO) noted need to vote on matter before tax
rate is set noting that setting a future tax levy is based on estimates but 
would not affect current rate.  C. Juran noted support as it would not 
increase taxes.  C. Juran noted it would not correct overtime wages in the 
short term.  Manager Golden, Jr. laid out the financial aspects of the vote 
and noted long term planning which would be affected by retirements and 
other occurrences in the department.  Mr. Baldwin noted time will tell 
regarding overtime use.  Manager Golden, Jr. Noted meetings with fire

Registered speaker, Bill Harland (LFD Union) voiced his support of the vote
and commented on hiring process for new fire fighters.  C. Scott noted 
effect of retirements on staffing in the department.  Mr. Baldwin noted it is 
best if there is advanced notice of retirements but that does not always 
happen but there seems to be 3-4 per year.  C. Robinson noted contract 
with union is due next year.  C. Descoteaux commented on training for new 
fire fighters and noted concern for overtime.  C. Mercier noted support of 
the vote and the need to hire in the department.  C. McDonough noted 
better time is to discuss these matters when developing the budget.  Chair 
released to Vice Chair Nuon at 8:02 PM.  M. Gitschier commented on the 
depletion of the staff and that vote would not reduce overtime wages.  M. 
Gitschier noted the City provides too many sick days to employees so they 
can expect overtime wages.  Chair returned at 8:09 PM.  C. Liang noted 
there is no quick relief for overtime wages and must see how it goes in the 
long run.  C. Robinson noted the need to streamline the hiring process.  C. 
Descoteaux requested LFD report regarding spending.  
Motion by C. Descoteaux, seconded by C. Chau to take Item #8.2 out of 
order.  So voted.  
6.4. Vote - Transfer $180,430 - PEG Fund.
In City Council, Given 2nd reading.  Motion “To Adopt” by C. Robinson, 
seconded by C. Juran.  Adopted per Roll Call vote 7 yeas (C. Chau, C. 
Descoteaux, M. Gitschier, C. Juran, C. Mercier, C. Nuon, C. Scott), 2 nays 
(C. McDonough, C. Robinson.  So voted.  C. McDonough questioned where
funds went.  Mr. Baldwin noted it was part of the Comcast Franchise 
Agreement and money would go to City and Lowell Telecommunications 
Corporation (LTC) for support of municipal programming.  C. McDonough 
noted that LTC still has not resolved contract with workers.  C. Liang noted

member.  C. Robinson commented on job contract with LTC.  Mr. Baldwin 
noted City was not privy to that contract.  Austin Ball (Asst. CFO) noted 
funds would go to costs to LTC for municipal programming.  Motion by C. 
McDonough, second by C. Robinson to reduce amount to $152,000.00.  
DEFEATED per Roll Call vote 3 yeas (M. Gitschier, C. McDonough, C. 
Robinson), 6 nays (C. Chau, C. Descoteaux, C. Juran, C. Mercier, C. Nuon,
C. Scott), 1 recuse (C. Liang).  So voted.

transfer was to support police infrastructure and resources and questioned 
amount remaining in Free Cash.  Mr. Baldwin indicated the total remaining 
and there were sufficient funds to complete scheduled projects.  C. 
Robinson questioned if vehicles have maintenance plan.  Dept. Supt. 
LeBlanc noted maintenance is done in-house and outlined the rotation of 
older vehicles.  C. McDonough noted reduction in number of vehicles 
should have been planned during budget talks.  Mr. Baldwin noted 
equipment is part of capital plan but indicated that police vehicles differ due
to excessive use and mileage.  C. Scott questioned age of vehicles when 
rotated and if transfer is for body cameras as well.  Dept. Supt. LeBlanc 
outlined rotation of vehicles and indicated that tasers are part of the funding
as well.  C. Descoteaux commented on the use of cameras.  Dept. Supt. 
LeBlanc noted contract allows for replacements.  Chair released to Vice 
Chair Nuon at 7:01 PM.  M. Gitschier stated that discussion and funding 
should have been done during budget session.  Dept. Supt. LeBlanc 
commented on the timing and the need for the funding and the savings that 
will be realized by this vote.  Motion by M. Gitschier, seconded by C. 
McDonough to refer matter to Finance SC.  After discussion motion was 
withdrawn by M. Gitschier with no objection by C. McDonough.  Chair 
returned at 7:07 PM.  C. Descoteaux questioned the remaining Free Cash.  
C. Robinson questioned if cemetery work would be affected by the transfer.
Mr. Baldwin indicated that the work was not funded by Free Cash.  C. Nuon
questioned if proper use of Free Cash.  Mr. Baldwin noted funds were being
reallocated and was within statute.  C. Mercier noted public safety is 
number one priority and that there is no effect on taxes.  C. McDonough 
noted concern with Free Cash and that issue should have been addressed 
at budget time.  C. Liang noted support but needed to know earlier.  C. 
Chau noted need to support police to ensure safety of the public.  C. Juran 
noted the immediate need for public safety but commented that such 
matters should go before the Finance SC.  C. Scott recognized the 
immediate need for the police and that same standard should apply for fire 
department.  Chair released to Vice Chair Nuon at 7:25 PM.  M. Gitschier 
commented that questions should be formulated at budget creating time.
